Trust our 250+ years of experience and top-tier reputation to help you get the results you deserve. How Much Is My Personal Injury Case Worth? Every personal injury case is different. However, several common factors will play a part in determining how much money you might be able to recover with a lawsuit. The following can impact what your case is worth: What types of physical injuries have you suffered? Are you still able to work? Has your earning capacity changed? What has your accident cost you out of pocket? Do you share responsibility for the accident or the severity of your injuries? What insurance benefits are available to you? What are the policy limits? What did you do to mitigate your damages? How old were you when you got hurt? How have your injuries changed your ability to live and enjoy your life? The type of injuries you’ve suffered and their severity will almost always be the most critical factor when assessing what your personal injury claim is worth. The more serious an injury, the more of a financial impact it’ll tend to have on your life. In turn, the higher your damages are, the more you will need financial support. However, there are factors that can limit your financial recovery, such as shared fault and a failure to mitigate damages. Learn more about what your personal injury case might be worth and increase the odds of a meaningful recovery by talking to an experienced California trial attorney near you. Why Should I Hire a Personal Injury Attorney in California? You’re more likely to win your personal injury case when you hire a lawyer. You’re also more likely to maximize your financial recovery. Here’s why: You force the insurance company to handle your claim in good faith and make genuine attempts to settle your claim for what it’s worth You benefit from the law firm’s considerable resources and network of expert witnesses The insurance company loses the upper hand and won’t be able to rely on unsubstantiated claims of shared fault to limit your payout You’ll have a legitimate idea about what your personal injury case is worth and know whether you’re being lowballed or extended a fair offer You’ll also have time to focus on recovering from your injuries and moving forward with your life. Your California personal injury attorney will handle everything else on your behalf. You have the power to decide which attorney you want to handle your personal injury case. Your choice matters. When you put The Simon Law Group in your corner, you send a clear message to the defense. You won’t be pushed around, and you won’t walk away with less than you deserve. Call one of our California law offices, conveniently located in Orange County and Los Angeles, to learn more. How Much Does It Cost to Hire a Personal Injury Lawyer? The Simon Law Group handles personal injury cases on contingency. Under our contingency fee structure, our clients pay nothing unless and until we win financial compensation on their behalf. If we don’t win, you pay nothing. When we do win, our fees, which are a percentage of your financial recovery, are dedicated right out of your personal injury award. What Types of Damages Can I Get With a Personal Injury Claim? In California, compensatory damages can be awarded to plaintiffs in successful personal injury disputes. Compensatory damages include two different types of awards. Economic damages help you handle the costs that arise because of your accident or injury, such as: Present and future medical bills Lost wages and income Disability Property damage Out-of-pocket expenses Rehabilitation Funeral expenses Non-economic damages help you deal with harder-to-value struggles that result from your accident or injury, such as: Pain and suffering Emotional distress Reduced quality of life Chronic physical pain Disfigurement Loss of consortium Embarrassment Punitive damages could also be on the table if your personal injury lawsuit goes to trial. However, in California, this is limited to situations where there’s proof of malice, oppression, or fraud. In other words, a jury would have to be convinced that the defendant acted intentionally or displayed a conscious disregard for your safety. How Could Comparative Fault Affect My California Personal Injury Settlement? California’s pure comparative negligence rule will limit your ability to recover compensation if you share some of the blame for your recent accident. Damages are reduced proportionately to fault. The more responsibility you share for your injuries, the more of an impact it’ll have on your financial recovery. If you’re assigned 25 percent of the blame for a recent auto accident in California, your settlement or jury award will be reduced by 25 percent. When Do I Have to File a Personal Injury Lawsuit in California? Most personal injury cases are subject to a two-year statute of limitations in the state of California. If you want to reserve the right to compensation from an insurer or party responsible for your accident, you must file your claim within the applicable statute of limitations. If you miss the deadline, you’ll have to handle the costs of your accident and injuries on your own.
